clue.text: Fiancée's at home being looked after

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', so the definition is the fiancée, the person one means to marry

parts.note: at home means in, as in 'staying in'
looked after means tended

explanation.surface: A bride-to-be is staying at home being cared for.
explanation.definitionFit: One's intended is a familiar noun for the person one is engaged to marry.

clue.text: Muscle complaint

definitions.meaning: brawn or muscular strength, as in 'put some of that into it'
a grumble or grievance, as in 'what's your problem with me?'

explanation.definitionFit: The word is informal both for muscular power and, as a noun or verb, for a grievance.

clue.text: Sailor in the hold

definitions.meaning: Admiral Horatio ..., Britain's most famous naval commander
a wrestling hold in which the arms are locked behind the opponent's neck

explanation.surface: A seaman is down below in the ship's cargo space.
explanation.definitionFit: The admiral of Trafalgar shares his surname with a wrestling grip, the full or half version.

clue.text: Waste a prize

parts.note: a trophy is a prize such as a cup

explanation.surface: Someone thinks it a waste to award a prize.
explanation.definitionFit: To waste away, as a muscle does from disuse, is the verb's medical sense.

clue.text: Think of son being corrupted in drink

indicators.note: in places the scrambled son inside the drink

parts.note: cider is an apple drink

indicators.note: corrupted means spoiled or altered, so the letters of son are rearranged

explanation.surface: A parent ponders a son going to the bad through alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drink' could be any beverage; here the apple drink is the container, and 'being corrupted' scrambles only the three-letter word.
explanation.definitionFit: To consider something is to think about it carefully, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Chosen agents died horribly

indicators.note: horribly suggests something mangled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Selected spies met grisly ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone designated has been picked or appointed for a role.

clue.text: Article on the New Style capital

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
taken as written
S is an abbreviation for style

explanation.surface: A piece about the latest fashion in a capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link: in a down answer A sits on top of the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Athens is the capital city of Greece.

clue.text: Profit from hobby

definitions.meaning: the return earned on money lent or invested
a pastime or pursuit one enjoys

explanation.surface: Someone makes money out of their pastime.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both money paid on savings and an activity one pursues for enjoyment.

clue.text: Extra time is apparent

parts.note: over means extra, as in 'left over'

explanation.surface: Added time in a match is plain for everyone to see.
explanation.definitionFit: Overt means openly shown, so it is apparent rather than hidden.

clue.text: Money from chapel funds

indicators.note: from tells us to take the letters out of the words chapel funds

explanation.surface: Cash comes out of the church's collection.
explanation.definitionFit: Pelf is a disparaging word for money or wealth, often ill-gotten.

clue.text: Betrays drunk — the worse from exposure

parts.note: to shop someone is British slang for informing on them
oiled is slang for drunk

explanation.surface: A drunk who informs on others ends up the worse for wear.
explanation.walkthrough: SHOP is British slang for betraying someone to the police.
explanation.definitionFit: Shop-soiled goods are dirty or faded from being displayed in a shop, so worse for exposure.

clue.text: More often than not it's rum, my lad!

parts.note: rum is old British slang for odd or strange
my lad, said by a parent, means son

explanation.surface: A father exclaims that it is usually a strange business.
explanation.definitionFit: A result that is odds-on is more likely than not, in betting terms.

clue.text: Bishop wears tie for fellow member

indicators.note: the tie wears the bishop, so its letters go inside the word for tie

parts.note: stalemate is a drawn position or deadlock, a tie
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A churchman puts on a tie to meet a colleague.
explanation.definitionFit: A stablemate is a horse from the same stable, figuratively a member of the same group.

clue.text: Fellow in robbery is a pleasure-seeker

indicators.note: in places the fellow inside the word for robbery

parts.note: a heist is a robbery
a don is a university fellow

explanation.surface: An academic involved in a theft is just out for kicks.
explanation.definitionFit: A hedonist lives for pleasure, a synonym for pleasure-seeker.

clue.text: Fish with associate in a perfect world

parts.note: the ide is a freshwater fish
an ally is an associate or partner

explanation.surface: Fishing with a friend would be paradise.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideally means in the best possible circumstances, as in a perfect world.

clue.text: Player arranged tune found in catalogue

indicators.note: found in puts the rearranged tune inside the word for catalogue

parts.note: a list is a catalogue

indicators.note: arranged, as music is, signals the letters of tune being reordered

explanation.surface: A musician's arrangement of a melody appears in a catalogue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Player' could suggest a sportsman, but the musical sense of 'arranged' and 'tune' points to a musician.
explanation.definitionFit: A lutenist plays the lute, so is a kind of musical player.

clue.text: Childish talk makes Penny upset

parts.note: to rattle someone is to upset them

explanation.surface: A child's chatter annoys a girl called Penny.
explanation.definitionFit: Prattle is foolish, childlike chatter.

clue.text: Fail to be troubled in rescue situation

indicators.note: troubled means disturbed, so the letters of fail to be are stirred up

explanation.surface: Things look bad for someone caught up in a rescue.
explanation.definitionFit: A lifeboat is the vessel used at sea in a rescue situation.

clue.text: Militia protecting our weapons store

indicators.note: protecting means the army surrounds the word our

parts.note: a militia is a citizen army
taken as written

explanation.surface: A citizen force guards the arsenal.
explanation.definitionFit: An armoury is a place where weapons are kept.

clue.text: Pagan I figure out in time

parts.note: to figure out or work out a sum is to do it
in time means later, eventually

explanation.surface: A heathen says he will work it all out eventually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'figure out' looks like an anagram signal but means DO, as in doing a calculation.
explanation.definitionFit: An idolater worships idols, so is a pagan in the old religious sense.

clue.text: Cynical about operations for illness

indicators.note: about means the word for cynical goes round operations

parts.note: dry, of humour, is wry or cynical
ops is short for operations

explanation.surface: A jaded view of surgery for a disease.
explanation.definitionFit: Dropsy is an old name for oedema, swelling caused by fluid, an illness.

clue.text: Fall asleep in eastern drama put on very loudly

parts.note: Noh, also spelt No, is classical Japanese drama
to do a show is to put it on
FF, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loudly

explanation.surface: Someone dozes off during a Japanese play staged at full volume.
explanation.definitionFit: To nod off is an idiom for drifting into sleep.

clue.text: Managed duty in the raw

indicators.note: managed means handled or worked on, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone did their job while naked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is part of the fodder, not a link; the definition is 'the raw', as in 'in the raw'.
explanation.definitionFit: The raw, as in sleeping in the raw, means a state of nakedness.

clue.text: Ordinary bitter makes one feel unwell

definitions.note: a noun described by what it does: something that makes one feel ill

parts.note: common means ordinary
bitter weather is very cold

explanation.surface: A plain pint of bitter beer upsets the stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bitter' suggests the British beer but means cold, as in a bitter wind.
explanation.definitionFit: A cold is a mild viral infection which leaves sufferers feeling poorly.

clue.text: Trainee meets one in the country

parts.note: a cub, as in cub reporter, is a trainee
a means one

explanation.surface: A novice joins someone else out in the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuba is a Caribbean island nation.

clue.text: Produce a whip

definitions.meaning: farm produce, the yield of a harvest
a riding whip with a short stock

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a harvest of grain and a short whip used in riding.

clue.text: Locates spectacles, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the word for spectacles is said aloud to give the entry

parts.note: sights are spectacles, things worth seeing

explanation.surface: Someone finds their glasses, we are told.
explanation.definitionFit: To site something is to locate or position it.

clue.text: Helping a liberal's thinking

parts.note: a ration is a helping or portion
L is the abbreviation for Liberal

explanation.surface: A portion of a liberal's thought.
explanation.definitionFit: A rational being is capable of reasoned thinking.
